---
title: Languages (i18n)
description: How a bundled plugin provides Chinese and English. Manifest strings get English versions in `i18n.en`, screen and widget text goes in a `defineStrings` table, dates go through the SDK formatters, and text for the model stays untranslated.
icon: Languages
---

The app is available in Simplified Chinese (`zh-Hans`) and English (`en`). Chinese is the source
language: you write every string in Chinese first and then add the English version. Users choose
跟随系统 (follow the system), 简体中文 or English in Settings.

Every bundled plugin **MUST** be complete in both languages. The test `plugins/i18n.test.ts` in the
plugins repository checks each plugin and fails when an English string is missing. This page covers
bundled plugins. A plugin document puts all its English text in the `i18n.en` section of its
manifest (see [Declarative plugins](/en/docs/build/declarative-plugins#the-manifest)).

## What gets translated

Text that people read is translated. Text that only the model reads, such as tool descriptions and
instructions, is written once and not translated.

| Text | Where | Translate? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Plugin `name`, `description` | `definePlugin` (Chinese) + `i18n.en` | Yes |
| Tool `title`s | `tools.<name>.title` + `i18n.en.tools.<name>.title` | Yes |
| Tool `summary` (plugin documents only) | `summary` in the tool file + `i18n.en.tools.<name>.summary` | Yes |
| Widget titles and descriptions | `contributes.widgets` + `i18n.en.widgets` | Yes |
| Screen titles | `contributes.screens` + `i18n.en.screens` | Yes |
| Settings rows | `contributes.settings` + `i18n.en.settings.<screen>` | Yes |
| Commands | `contributes.commands` + `i18n.en.commands.<name>` (`description`, `argHint`, `aliases`, `prompt`) | Yes |
| Data source titles | `dataSources` + `i18n.en.dataSources` | Yes |
| Provider names, hints, model names | `providers` + `i18n.en.providers` | Yes |
| Screen and widget text | `src/strings.ts` (`defineStrings`) | Yes |
| Tool `description`, `instructions`, `context`, tool results | For the model | **No** |

## Manifest overlay

The Chinese strings stay where they are in `definePlugin`. The English versions go in `i18n.en`.
This example is from the `shuttle` plugin:

```ts
definePlugin({
  id: 'shuttle',
  name: '校车',
  description: '燕园—新燕园（昌平）通勤班车和新燕园—地铁北安河快速公交时刻表，算出下一班车。',
  i18n: {
    en: {
      name: 'Shuttle bus',
      description: 'Timetables for the Yanyuan–Xinyanyuan (Changping) commuter shuttle and the Xinyanyuan–Bei’anhe metro express bus, with the next departure worked out for you.',
      tools: { next: { title: 'Next shuttle' }, timetable: { title: 'Shuttle timetable' } },
      widgets: { next: { title: 'Next shuttle', description: '…' } },
      commands: { shuttle: { description: 'Next shuttle (works offline)', argHint: 'e.g. Yanyuan to Xinyanyuan', aliases: ['bus'] } },
      dataSources: { next: { title: 'Next shuttle' } },
    },
  },
  // …
});
```

At runtime, anything missing from `en` falls back to Chinese. The coverage test still fails, so fill
in everything.

## String tables

Text inside screens and widgets lives in a string table, one per plugin, in `src/strings.ts`. You
define its keys once as a type, then give a value for each language:

```ts title="src/strings.ts"
import { defineStrings } from '@pku-harness/sdk';

type Strings = {
  none: string;
  later: (list: string) => string;
};

export const strings = defineStrings<Strings>({
  'zh-Hans': { none: '今明两天没有班次', later: (list) => `之后 ${list}` },
  en: { none: 'No buses today or tomorrow', later: (list) => `Then ${list}` },
});
```

```tsx
const s = strings[host.useLocale()];
<Text>{s.none}</Text>
```

In a component, pick the table for the user's language with `host.useLocale()`.

`defineStrings` type-checks `en` against `zh-Hans`, so both need the same keys with the same value
types. A string with parameters is a function. Never build a sentence by joining translated
fragments, because word order differs between the two languages.

## Dates and numbers

Hermes, the JavaScript engine the app runs on, ignores `Intl` locales. `toLocaleDateString` and
similar functions therefore give the wrong format. Use the SDK formatters instead. Most of them take
the locale `l` from `host.useLocale()`:

| Function | zh-Hans | en |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `formatClock(d)` | `21:04` | `21:04` |
| `formatWeekday(d, l)` | `周一` | `Mon` |
| `formatLocalDate(d, l)` | `10月18日` | `Oct 18` |
| `formatLocalDateTime(d, l)` | `10月18日 21:04` | `Oct 18, 21:04` |
| `formatRelative(ms, l)` | `刚刚`, `3 分钟前`, `昨天 21:04` | `Just now`, `3 min ago`, `Yesterday 21:04` |
| `formatDay(d, l)` | `今天`, `明天`, `周三` | `Today`, `Tomorrow`, `Wed` |
| `formatCountdown(ms, l)` | `2小时10分` | `2h 10m` |
| `plural(n, one)` | — | `1 book`, `3 books` |

Details in [SDK → format](/en/docs/sdk/format).

## English copy rules

The coverage test also checks how English strings are written:

- No Chinese except inside a parenthesised gloss or quotes. `Treehole (树洞)` is fine.
- Curly apostrophes (`’`), not straight ones (`'`).
- No exclamation marks.
- Keep it short and in sentence case, which capitalises only the first word and proper nouns.
  Campus proper nouns use the official English name or pinyin: Peking University, Treehole (树洞),
  Course (教学网 / Blackboard), Campus Card.

Chinese text follows the same idea: keep it short and use no exclamation marks.
